evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Terminal sessions and dev sessions have explicit restore eligibility; running processes are never assumed alive after restart, and terminal restart or replacement creates a new terminal_session_id.

items.impact: Implementations can disagree about which sessions qualify for restore and how eligibility is proven, risking false live-state presentation after restart.
items.statement: The identity reset and no-fake-liveness rules are explicit, but the eligibility inputs, decision record, failure reasons, and executable restore oracle are not specified.
items.title: Restore eligibility lacks a decision contract

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Terminal section, tab, pane, selection-of-active-pane, labels, pin state, dock/detach placement, and linked dev-session references are guaranteed_durable presentation metadata.

items.impact: Concurrent pane, detach, pin, and dev-session updates can restore an internally inconsistent presentation without ordering or atomicity rules.
items.statement: The durable field set is exact, but versioning, write ordering, atomic grouping, dangling-reference handling, and rollback semantics remain unspecified.
items.title: Durable presentation metadata has no atomicity model

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Terminal transcript snapshots, command-block metadata, cwd snapshots, shell-integration hints, and Output/Ports linkage are best_effort_durable, while live PTY continuity, unlimited scrollback, TUI alternate-screen content, live selections, and in-flight search highlights are transient_only.

items.impact: Storage, privacy, and restore behavior cannot be tested consistently when durability, retention, pruning, and redaction bounds are left open.
items.statement: The persistence tiers are explicit, but best_effort_durable has no minimum guarantee, retention cap, pruning disclosure, redaction lifecycle, or failure receipt.
items.title: Best-effort terminal durability is not bounded

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Canonical restore outcomes are exactly restored_live, restored_exited, restored_disconnected, and restored_without_history.

items.impact: The same runtime condition may map to different outcome tokens or GUI actions, making recovery behavior misleading and hard to falsify.
items.statement: The vocabulary is closed, but entry criteria, allowed transitions, terminality, reason codes, and required user actions for each outcome are absent.
items.title: Restore tokens lack state semantics

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Promotion from paused automation into normal browsing is an explicit user-confirmed action that may copy or promote eligible browser state, reclassifies the visible automation browser as normal, and is never a hidden side effect.

items.impact: A partial copy or interrupted reclassification can leak state, duplicate credentials, or leave the browser's displayed class inconsistent with its authority.
items.statement: Explicit consent is well constrained, but eligible state, consent scope, copy atomicity, interruption recovery, audit receipt, revocation, and source cleanup are not defined.
items.title: Browser promotion lacks transactional privacy rules

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Browser requested/effective runtime and capability state is stored as frozen runtime history instead of recomputed heuristically, and crash recovery preserves recoverable metadata and completed evidence artifacts when possible.

items.impact: The phrase when possible permits silent evidence loss and prevents deterministic crash-recovery acceptance tests.
items.statement: Frozen history is a strong non-heuristic rule, but recoverability criteria, commit boundaries, corruption behavior, loss receipts, and reconciliation after crash are unspecified.
items.title: Crash evidence preservation remains non-falsifiable

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Browser or terminal session classes must not silently bleed storage into another profile scope, and profile { name, saveChanges } scopes cookies and localStorage by profile name and project while disabled saveChanges keeps the session isolated.

items.impact: Undefined normalization, deletion, collision, and concurrent-write behavior can violate profile isolation despite the stated boundary.
items.statement: The project-plus-profile boundary and disabled-save isolation are explicit, but profile-name identity, other storage classes, encryption, disposal, migration, and concurrent writers are not covered.
items.title: Profile storage isolation lacks lifecycle closure

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The title-bar project bar, floating thread-selector overlay, and detached usage pop-out are explicitly non-canonical promoted shell, thread navigation, and per-thread usage models.

items.impact: Builders and migration tooling have an unambiguous prohibition against reviving the three retired GUI surfaces as canonical behavior.
items.statement: The retired shell, thread-navigation, and usage surfaces are named and explicitly declared non-canonical, with owner hints for seam checks.
items.title: Retired shell surfaces are explicitly bounded

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: One broad browser-instance model with LRU reuse is not the core browser contract.

items.impact: The negative rule prevents one design but does not determine isolation, pooling, eviction, resource limits, or ownership for the promoted model.
items.statement: The LRU-wide-instance model is excluded, but no positive browser-instance lifecycle or capacity contract is supplied in this unit.
items.title: Browser instance non-goal lacks a positive contract

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The bottom panel is not the primary browser host for the promoted browser model.

items.impact: Builders can choose incompatible primary hosts and responsive behavior while still satisfying the negative placement rule.
items.statement: Bottom-panel primacy is prohibited, but the authoritative browser host, detach behavior, small-window fallback, and ownership boundary are unstated.
items.title: Promoted browser host remains ambiguous

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Ordinary browser clicks or text selection must not silently inject context into assistant prompts or runtime state.

items.impact: Without a positive share contract, adapters may use inconsistent consent, provenance, redaction, and revocation behavior around untrusted page content.
items.statement: Silent injection is clearly prohibited, but explicit sharing inputs, confirmation scope, provenance receipt, target consumers, redaction, and cancellation are not defined.
items.title: Browser context sharing has only a prohibition

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Silent storage bleed between browser session classes or profile scopes is non-canonical.

items.impact: The prohibition can pass prose validation while cross-scope reads or writes remain undetected at runtime and in tests.
items.statement: The privacy boundary is explicit, but the enumerated storage surfaces, isolation key, detection telemetry, denial receipt, and adversarial cross-scope oracle are missing.
items.title: Storage-bleed prohibition lacks enforcement evidence

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Raw CDP or arbitrary browser code execution is not the guaranteed core browser contract.

items.impact: Optional adapters could expose low-level execution without a common permission, sandbox, provenance, or compatibility boundary.
items.statement: Raw CDP and arbitrary execution are excluded from the guaranteed core, but the conditions under which they may exist and the required safety boundary are unspecified.
items.title: Non-core browser execution remains under-bounded

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Generic watch mode is not the primary dev-loop model.

items.impact: Consumers cannot determine which event source, restart policy, debouncing, or failure behavior is canonical for the primary dev loop.
items.statement: The non-goal is clear, but the positive primary dev-loop model and its callers, transitions, and operational oracles are absent from the unit.
items.title: Dev-loop non-goal does not name the primary model

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: MCP is not config-and-passthrough only; Section 15 consumers rely on host-managed MCP capability resolution.

items.impact: Hosts may resolve capabilities with incompatible authority, caching, revocation, fallback, or offline semantics.
items.statement: Host-managed capability resolution is required, but request and result shapes, precedence, permission snapshot, cache lifetime, revocation propagation, and network-loss behavior are undefined.
items.title: Host-managed MCP resolution lacks a lifecycle contract

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: App-level-only tool permission scope is insufficient for the promoted project-switch, MCP, and browser model.

items.impact: Permission checks can diverge at project switches and across browser or MCP consumers, causing over-grant or stale authority.
items.statement: The app-only scope is rejected, but required scope levels, inheritance, conflict precedence, switch invalidation, snapshot identity, and consumer enforcement are not specified.
items.title: Tool permission hierarchy is unspecified

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Stale Persona/tier selectors from Personas.md, Contracts_V0, and Contracts_V0.md, including _persona_id and select_for_tier(), are not canonical promoted-shell fields; Section 15 consumers use requested/effective Persona identity and runtime owner scope instead.

items.impact: Existing persisted or adapter payloads can retain stale selector authority or map inconsistently to requested and effective identity.
items.statement: Replacement identity concepts are named, but legacy-field detection, mapping, rejection, telemetry, version cutoff, and migration acceptance cases are not defined.
items.title: Retired Persona selectors lack migration mechanics

evidence.exact_quote: - VT replay corpus includes OSC 52/8/9;4/133/633, bracketed paste, focus, mouse, alternate screen, synchronized update sequences.

items.impact: The corpus can exist without byte-exact expected state, malformed-sequence behavior, resource ceilings, or a completeness rule for negotiation combinations.
items.statement: The required protocol families and cross-platform determinism are strong, but fixture schemas, expected parser and screen outputs, malformed-input cases, timeout and memory ceilings, and negotiation coverage are not closed.
items.title: Terminal protocol matrix lacks full executable fixture semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - A fast-output fixture records byte counts and no silent loss.

items.impact: Different implementations may drop, defer, throttle, or block at incompatible points while each claims that receipts account for output.
items.statement: Lifecycle stages and record minima are enumerated, but queue bounds, high and low watermarks, ordering, overflow policy, counter reconciliation, UI status thresholds, and recovery after saturation are absent.
items.title: Terminal backpressure has receipts but no control law

evidence.exact_quote: - Screen reader projection can read current line, selection, prompt/command boundaries, and latest output without scraping GPU pixels.

items.impact: Screen readers can receive stale, excessively noisy, unredacted, or incorrectly segmented terminal content despite the separate text model.
items.statement: The readable projection and spam throttling goals are explicit, but update events, focus and cursor semantics, latency, announcement modes and thresholds, redaction, Unicode segmentation, and localization behavior are not specified.
items.title: Terminal accessibility mirror lacks event semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - Pasting mixed URL/plain text chooses plain text unless user selects URI action.

items.impact: Dangerous or remote clipboard data may be handled differently across sources, contexts, and repeated approvals, leaving command-execution and privacy risk.
items.statement: Priority and key safety outcomes are stated, but exact dangerous-character classification, normalization preview, approval lifetime, remote trust derivation, OSC 52 directionality, denial receipts, and cancellation are open.
items.title: Clipboard safety lacks a complete policy state machine

evidence.exact_quote: - If live PTY cannot survive, UI says review-limited and offers restart/rerun, not fake continuity.

items.impact: Live-versus-historical behavior remains builder-dependent for local PTY, WSL, SSH, container, and devcontainer sessions, risking false continuity or missing recovery actions.
items.statement: The unit asks for a platform restore policy and honest review-limited GUI, but supplies no actual per-platform capability matrix, reconnect-token schema, timeout, failure taxonomy, banner copy, or transition table.
items.title: Terminal restore policy is requested but not specified

evidence.exact_quote: - OSC133 markers spanning multi-row prompt produce one region

items.impact: Malformed, nested, pane-forwarded, or reordered markers can create contradictory command regions or overstate semantic confidence.
items.statement: Confidence tiers and key parser cases are named, but marker grammar, region lifecycle, duplicate and nested marker precedence, pane visibility, downgrade transitions, and persisted confidence provenance are not defined.
items.title: Semantic marker confidence lacks conflict rules

evidence.exact_quote: - No control sequence bytes leak to visible grid when split across reads

items.impact: An attacker or faulty process can hold parser state indefinitely, consume unbounded memory, or trigger inconsistent recovery without violating the byte-split fixtures.
items.statement: Every-byte-boundary fuzzing is strong, but maximum pending-sequence size, timeout or EOF behavior, invalid-byte recovery, diagnostic receipt, and post-error resynchronization are missing.
items.title: Chunk-spanning parser lacks bounded failure recovery

evidence.exact_quote: - Accessibility visible range returns viewport, not full scrollback

items.impact: Range queries may return inconsistent text and bounds during output or resize, leak redacted content, or exceed acceptable latency despite being O(viewport).
items.statement: Viewport scoping and redaction awareness are explicit, but snapshot identity, index units, mutation consistency, bounds coordinate space, stale-range behavior, quantitative latency, and Unicode grapheme semantics are absent.
items.title: Accessibility ranges lack snapshot and index semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - Doctor detects incompatible ConPTY pair

items.impact: Diagnostics may expose sensitive host details, become stale, or produce non-actionable and inconsistent degradation results across platforms.
items.statement: Useful provenance fields and doctor outcomes are named, but collection authority, redaction, freshness, version comparison source, reason-code vocabulary, localization, and remediation actions are unspecified.
items.title: Terminal doctor lacks privacy and remediation semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - Terminal byte stream preserves parser state across chunks

items.impact: A UI transport can reconnect, duplicate, drop, or reorder byte frames without a specified way to preserve parser correctness or disclose loss.
items.statement: The separation of PTY bytes, parser state, scrollback, model excerpts, and UI transport is explicit, but framing, sequence identity, delivery guarantees, reconnect, backpressure, corruption, and excerpt authorization are not.
items.title: PTY stream separation lacks delivery semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - Running a high-output TUI agent does not freeze GUI or explode logs.

items.impact: Agent-mode detection and throttling can vary, causing GUI freezes, memory or log growth, lost output, or accidental elevation of terminal text to trusted receipts.
items.statement: The control categories and no-fake-receipt rule are strong, but agent detection authority, output-rate classes, numeric budgets, suppression accounting, recovery hysteresis, detached continuation, and user override semantics are missing.
items.title: Agent output storm controls are not quantitatively bounded

evidence.exact_quote: - Terminal paste/drop/autofill inputs pass through TerminalInputSanitizer with control-code stripping/escaping policy and user-visible preview for dangerous content.

items.impact: OTP, autofill, pasteboard, drag/drop, and file URL data can leak or execute under inconsistent approval and sanitization rules.
items.statement: The sanitizer, blocking, preview, explicit approval, and FileSafe gates are explicit, but channel classification, sanitization transformation, approval granularity and lifetime, secure preview, audit retention, cancellation, and TOCTOU behavior are not.
items.title: Sensitive OS channels lack approval lifecycle details

evidence.exact_quote: - IME candidate follows cursor cell

items.impact: IME composition, Unicode graphemes, key repeat, global bindings, pasteboard flavors, and viewport mutations can diverge by platform and locale.
items.statement: Three acceptance examples exist, but the platform and locale fixture matrix, composition state transitions, grapheme indexing, keybinding precedence, cancellation, pasteboard trust cases, and clear or cls oracle are not enumerated.
items.title: Terminal input and IME matrix is only partially specified

evidence.exact_quote: Terminal lessons from Ghostty, Warp, tmux, and CLI tools apply only to Puppet Master built-in GUI terminal/runtime contracts. They must not create a PM CLI product, make terminal the PM control plane, or mint pseudo-terminals outside terminal_session_id ownership.

items.impact: The imported terminal lessons cannot expand product scope, displace Puppet Master authority, or bypass terminal session ownership.
items.statement: The GUI-terminal-only scope, no-PM-CLI rule, no-terminal-control-plane rule, and terminal_session_id ownership guard are explicit and independently testable as negative constraints.
items.title: Terminal import authority guardrails are explicit

segments.summary: Reviewed terminal restore identity, durable presentation metadata, persistence tiers, restore vocabulary, browser promotion, and crash evidence with exact and adversarial lifecycle lenses.
Reviewed profile isolation, retired shell surfaces, browser-instance and host non-goals, context injection, storage bleed, and low-level execution boundaries.
Reviewed dev-loop, MCP resolution, and tool-permission scope non-goals against positive-contract and authority-boundary needs.
Reviewed stale Persona selector disposition and the surrounding migration-only bridge and coverage constraints for compatibility ambiguity.

Reviewed protocol fixtures, browser action and timeout repairs, tab restore, layout transform, usage compatibility, terminal record minima, runtime packaging, backpressure, accessibility, and clipboard safety.
Reviewed terminal restore, semantic markers, chunk-spanning parsing, accessibility ranges, and host provenance across failure, concurrency, performance, and GUI-truth dimensions.
Reviewed PTY stream separation, agent output storms, sensitive OS channels, IME and pasteboard behavior, and terminal product-authority guardrails.

cross_document_questions: Which owner document defines the positive browser-instance lifecycle and authoritative primary browser host excluded by SMPFS-115 and SMPFS-116?
Where is the complete tool-permission scope hierarchy and project-switch invalidation contract consumed by browser and MCP resolution?
Which storage and GUI contracts own transactional browser promotion, crash-evidence preservation, and terminal restore outcome semantics?
Where are PTY transport delivery, parser resource ceilings, terminal backpressure thresholds, and user-visible loss receipts jointly closed?
